News.title: Mystery of WW1 shipwreck solved after 108 years as Brit divers make staggering deep-sea discovery
News.content:
A TEAM of intrepid British divers have solved the 108-year mystery of the sinking of a US coastguard cutter in its largest naval loss of World War I.

The wreck of the Tampa – blown up by a German submarine in 1918 with the loss of all 131 hands – was found after a painstaking three year search and 10 unsuccessful dives.





Dom Robinson, 54, was among the technical dive crew to find the famous US ship 50 miles off the coast of Cornwall.

The former Army chopper pilot told how the wreck was found 95m down on the seabed.

He said: “It’s the culmination of an awful lot of work.

“This was the moment we dreamed of.



“We had almost given up and this was the last dive we were going to do.”

The Tampa was escorting a convoy into the Irish Sea when it split off into the Bristol Channel to refuel and was torpedoed by a Kaiser sub and sank within three minutes.



A total of 111 Coast Guardsmen, four US Navy personnel, and 16 Royal Navy sailors and civilians perished.

The wreck location was only roughly known from a combination of German and British records and from data from the UK Hydrographic Society.

The US Coast Guard contributed details to help identify the ship.

Dom, and the group of divers from the South West area, who call themselves the Gasperadoes, finally managed to pinpoint the exact location after three years of looking.

He said: “We are really pleased we found it.



“We had a rough idea of where it was.

“Each time it takes three hours to drive out there, you’re in the water for 20 mins, and then there’s two-and-a-half hours of decompression and then travel back again.

“It’s a super niche activity and quite expensive.

“The ship was quite small and we were lucky to find it.”

The US Coast Guard said it is now planning to send a ship over to lay a wreath on the wreck site.



The force’s commandant, Admiral Kevin Lunday, said: “Since 1790, the Coast Guard has defended our nation during every armed conflict in American history, a legacy reflected in the courage and sacrifice of the crew of Coast Guard Cutter Tampa.

“When the Tampa was lost with all hands in 1918, it left an enduring grief in our service.

“Locating the wreck connects us to their sacrifice and reminds us that devotion to duty endures.

“We will always remember them.

“We are proud to carry their spirit forward in defense of the United States.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Coast Guard Atlantic Area Historian, Dr William Thiesen, said: “We provided the dive team with historical records and technical data to assist in confirming the wreck site.

“This included the archival images of the deck fittings, ship’s wheel, bell , weaponry, and archival images of the Tampa.”

News.title: ‘Death trap’ houses in seaside town are covered in rubbish & have rat infestation as locals fear people could die
News.content:
'KEEP CLEAR' ‘Death trap’ houses in seaside town are covered in rubbish & have rat infestation as locals fear people could die

“DEATH trap” houses with piles of rubbish stacked on roofs have left residents of a seaside town fearing someone will be killed.

The bizarre looking properties in Blyth, Northumberland, have left locals fearing rodents and faeces may be lurking inside.





The ramshackle buildings have kitchen cupboard doors nailed over windows alongside signs which read “keep clear” and “permit to work must be obtained”.

One of the houses has a huge mound on what appears to be the roof of a garage formed from ladders, a trolley, multiple planks and other debris.

The property opposite on Carlton Street has a mural depicting a child skipping, two women holding flags as well as the name of the owner, Henry John Knox Cleave, who is known as John.

Amongst the rubbish are colourful flowers, which are clearly being tended to, but locals have slammed the properties as “dangerous” and “disgusting” and urged the council to act.



Aerial pictures show the scale of the junk littering the roofs of the properties.

Sam Kennedy, 21, a hospitality supervisor, said: “It’s absolutely awful. The number of storms we’ve had, I am surprised they’re still standing, when we’ve had fences blown off.



“It’s an accident waiting to happen. Everyone avoids walking close to the houses in case something falls off them.

“If the outside is anything to go by, the inside must be minging. Totally dirty.

“It’s really unsafe and the council should do something about it.



“I’ve lived here all my life and for as long as I can remember the houses have always been like that and it’s getting worse and worse.

“Blyth has a bad name anyway, and those houses have almost become a landmark. It’s ridiculous. It’s terrible.”

Full-time mum Lucillia Fox, 22, added: “These houses just make Blyth look scruffy.

“Getting the bus to the beach, and seeing that, it makes us look like scruffs.

“I am definitely annoyed by it. All the rubbish has been like that for the three years I have been here.



“More and more is piling up. We won’t even park there in case something falls on the car.

“It just takes the bad winds for something to fall off.

“It could kill someone and it’s getting worse and worse.

“I don’t even want to imagine what it’s like inside. There will be rats, rubbish and faeces.”

Another resident who didn’t want to be named said: “It’s really dangerous. Like a death trap.



“It’s horrendous, especially with the high winds.

“I think it should be taken down, the whole lot.

“If for some reason it collapses while someone is walking past, they could be killed.”

There are two properties on Carlton Street, one on nearby Gladstone Street and a fourth on Beaumont Street. Locals say John Cleave, who we were unable to contact for comment, also owns further houses in the town.

A spokesperson for Northumberland County Council said: “We are aware of these properties. At present, our focus is on 33 Carlton Street, where a Section 215 notice was served.



“The notice required the removal of various items from the elevations and roof of the property. The notice was appealed and dismissed at the Magistrates’ Court.

“A further appeal was made to the Crown Court, where some amendments were made to the notice; however, the appeal was again dismissed overall. Following the appeal decision, the Section 215 notice took effect, and the requirements of the notice were required to be complied with by a specified date.

“This has not occurred. The council now has the option to either pursue prosecution for non‑compliance or to arrange for the required works to be carried out directly, with the costs secured as a land charge against the property.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In May last year, Mr Cleave was fined £400 and ordered to pay £1,868.41 in costs at Newcastle Magistrates’ Court after being found guilty of failing to comply with a community protection notice he had been issued the previous year. The notice was for him to remove the items/waste in the rear lane of Carlton Street.

Council officials were at the property today and said they wanted to speak to John about an unrelated matter.

News.title: Golders Green ‘knifeman’ was once accused of stabbing two cops & police dog with ex-PC saying ‘I’m lucky to be here’
News.content:
KNIFE SUSPECT FLAGGED Golders Green ‘knifeman’ was once accused of stabbing two cops & police dog with ex-PC saying ‘I’m lucky to be here’

THE man arrested over the Golders Green knife rampage was once accused of stabbing two officers and a police dog, it emerged last night.

Essa Suleiman, 45, was recently freed from a psychiatric unit under the Government’s Care in the Community programme — leading to questions about the supervision of the terror suspect.





Met commissioner Sir Mark Rowley said at the scene of the attacks the suspect had a history of violence and mental illness.

The Met also revealed yesterday that concerns were raised about Suleiman’s extremist beliefs and that he was referred to the Prevent programme in 2020.

A source said the knife attack in North West London had “shades of the Nottingham and Southport attacks”.

The UK terror threat level was last night raised from “substantial” to “severe” — meaning an attack within the next six months was rated as “highly likely”.



Suleiman, a British citizen who came to this country from Somalia as a child in the 1990s, is said to have regularly attended pro-Palestinian demos in London.

And it has emerged the former school security guard was once accused of a vicious knife attack while under the influence of drugs in Swindon, Wilts, in 2008.



Two officers, including PC Neil Sampson and his dog Anya, were attacked by a man with a huge knife, leaving PC Sampson needing 30 stitches for wounds to his head, face and leg.

German shepherd Anya was stabbed but made a full recovery.

Dad and grandad Neil — who has now retired after 28 years on the job — told The Sun last night: “I was stabbed seven times. I had a police dog biting him, I had colleagues coming in and helping, and he was being batoned, he was being sprayed, he was tasered.



“I thought he was punching me in the back of the head.

“But it was him stabbing me in the back of the head. When I say I’m lucky to be here, if that had hit the femoral artery, I’d be saying bye-bye.”

Sources said Suleiman was under the care of mental health services before the attacks on two Jewish men on Wednesday.



Rabbi Solomon Rand, 34, was stabbed in the chest, with his heart narrowly missed, and 76-year-old Moshe Shine was stabbed in the neck at a bus stop.

Mr Rand, from Stamford Hill, North London, told the BBC: “I’ve had a stab to my chest, and, yes, my lungs have to recover.

“I hope I’ll be better soon.”

He called on the Government — which yesterday pledged an extra £25million to protect the Jewish community — to “pull their socks up” to tackle antisemitism, saying: “It can no longer be ignored by the Government.

“People are afraid.”



The national terror threat level was raised to severe yesterday by the Government’s Joint Terrorism Analysis Centre over concerns about Islamist and extreme right-wing individuals and groups.

Last night police were still questioning Suleiman after his arrest on suspicion of attempted murder.

Counter-terror police are leading the inquiry with MI5.

One source said: “The Golders Green attack has shades of Nottingham and Southport in as much as the suspect was known to mental health services.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Southport killer Axel Rudakubana was also referred to Prevent and had been discharged from mental health services six days before he murdered three young girls at a dance class in 2024.



Paranoid schizophrenic Valdo Calocane had been under the care of ­Nottinghamshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust before he killed Barnaby Webber, Grace ­O’Malley-Kumar and Ian Coates in 2023.

News.title: PM can stuff ‘thoughts & prayers’ where the sun don’t shine… If he really cared about Jews’ suffering he’d DO something
News.content:
TWO British men are lying in hospital after being brutally stabbed simply for being Jewish, and the “thoughts and prayers” are now flowing thick and fast.

Once again, Sir Keir Starmer, the Met Police chief, London Mayor and all the usual suspects have lined up to lecture us about our “British values”, the need for “solidarity” and to tell us just how “shocked and appalled” they are.





Well, sorry, but I’m not remotely shocked by yet another antisemitic attack.

Frankly, Prime Minister, you can stuff your “thoughts and prayers”, and you can take your “don’t look back in anger” ­cliches and shove them where the sun don’t shine.

I’m done with all the hand-wringing platitudes and the promises of action every time we face another terror attack on our streets.

It’s long past time for our ­politicians and police to ACT.

They keep telling us that “antisemitism has no place in Britain”.

But that’s a lie.



Jew-hatred most definitely DOES have a place in Britain.

Indeed, it’s now rampant on our streets, in our schools and universities, in the NHS, in our political parties, in the media and all over our social media.

The oldest hatred in the world has moved from the fringes of the Far Right to the mainstream of the so-called “progressive” Left.

What were once shocking views shouted by Nazi skinheads are now the norm among far too many people who proclaim themselves as “anti-racist” and “anti-fascist”.

Yet even while the likes of Starmer ­cannot shy away from acknowledging the antisemitism that is exploding across our country, the Prime Minister — like most of our politicians — dodges any mention of how it happened.



Because the elephant — indeed the big HERD of elephants — in the room that everyone is ignoring is that this is a ­problem we have imported from overseas.

Yes, antisemitism has always existed in Britain, but it has been turbo-charged by the arrival of millions in the past few decades from ­cultures where hatred of Jews is not the exception, it’s the norm.

Just ask yourself: who is being charged with all of these antisemitic crimes and terror attacks?

Is it Brenda Bloggs from Somerset?

Is it John Smith from ­Norwich?



No, it’s mostly Islamist extremists who are first or second-generation immigrants from Muslim countries where antisemitism is rife.

That’s not bigotry, that’s just fact.

Yet the PM, in a statement from Downing Street, where he had escaped after being loudly booed and jeered during a visit to Golders Green, made NOT ONE mention of Islamist extremism.

How can you tackle the problem if you can’t even identify what the cause is?

The suspect in the latest attack in ­Golders Green is Essa Suleiman, a 45-year-old man described by the police as a “British national, born in Somalia”.



Of course, a more accurate description would be “a Somalian, living in Britain and given citizenship”.

We also now know he came to Britain as a child, had mental health issues, had been referred to the Prevent counter- extremism programme (another one of their many successes) and had a long ­history of serious violent offences.

If he is charged and convicted, Reform UK have called for this man to be stripped of his British citizenship and deported. And why not?

Why, you might ask, was he still here?

We keep being told that “diversity is our strength” but that’s just not true.



Britain’s strength is that we have a SHARED ­history, a shared culture, shared values and shared beliefs.

And tolerating those who are intolerant of those values is our greatest weakness.

But for far too long, the intolerance fuelled by Islamist extremism HAS been tolerated — and even pandered to by our politicians, in return for votes, and by our police, in return for peace on our streets.

Now we — but mostly the Jewish community — are paying the price for that.

There isn’t space on this page to list all the attacks on Jews in the past few months.



We’ve seen Jewish school-children facing abuse on the bus and intimidation of Jewish ­students on university campuses.

Jewish-owned businesses have been daubed with slogans or had their windows smashed.

Then there’s the spate of arson attacks, including the firebombing of a Jewish ­ambulance charity and, of course, the Heaton Park synagogue attack last October which left two men dead.

And then we have the fortnightly pro-Palestinian marches where antisemitism is openly on display on placards and banners and in chants over loudhailers as the police often stand by and do nothing.

Is it any wonder that the Islamist extremists think they can abuse and threaten Jews and non-Jews with impunity when the authorities appease rather than prosecute their crimes?



What about the Batley grammar school teacher in hiding with his family for five years for simply showing a cartoon of Mohammed to his pupils?

Not a single criminal charge has been brought against the Islamists who made death threats against him.

And the Wakefield boy who scuffed a Koran at school and whose mum, clad in a hijab, was taken by the local police chief to beg local Muslim leaders to help spare her son’s life?

What about the men who drove through London in 2021 in broad daylight shouting “F*** the Jews, f*** their mothers, rape their daughters and free Palestine”, none of whom were prosecuted?

And the rapper Bob Vylan who led chants of “death, death to the IDF” at Glastonbury last summer but faced no charges?



And the Muslim leaders who warned of mob violence if the visiting Israeli ­football team Maccabi Tel Aviv played in Birmingham?

Instead of arresting the mob, the police banned the Israeli fans instead.

The list of threats to Jews and to wider British society from the Islamist mob is endless but, while the solution isn’t quick or easy, it is SIMPLE.

Yes, of course we should proscribe Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and ban the Muslim Brotherhood and any other organisation that supports Islamist extremism.

But we also need to ban — and, where possible, deport — the hate preachers who are spouting their bile in mosques up and down the country.



The fortnightly pro-Palestinian marches through London must be stopped, unless or until the organisers can guarantee an end to the blatantly antisemitic chants and placards.

Sorry, folks, but the right to free speech and to protest doesn’t include the right to call for the death of Jews.

Because that is what “Globalise the ­intifada” means.

We need to prosecute each and every antisemitic abuser with severe punishments to send out a clear message that this behaviour will no longer be tolerated.

We need to deport any foreign citizens living in this country who support and encourage violence against Jews (or ­anyone else, for that matter).



And we must root out the antisemitism that has infected our schools, our universities, the NHS — and, yes, the BBC which has pumped out a never-ending stream of Islamist propaganda against Israel as uniquely evil, filling our airwaves with lies about genocide and famine in Gaza that have fanned the flames of Jew-hatred here, thinly disguised as the more socially acceptable “anti-Zionism”.

First and foremost, though, the so-called “progressive Left” among this Labour ­Government, as well as the Lib Dems and Zack Polanski’s Greens need to stop ­pandering to Islamist “Muslim community leaders” in return for their votes.

In his Downing Street statement, Starmer called for “everyone decent in this country” to “open their eyes to Jewish pain, Jewish suffering and Jewish fear” and urged “everyone to come together and fight antisemitism”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

That’s a laudable sentiment but fine words aren’t going to stop the next crazed knife attack on British Jews on our streets.

If the Prime Minister REALLY cares about Jewish suffering, then he needs to stop the talking and start DOING ­something about it.

News.title: If Starmer is serious about ‘opening eyes to Jewish pain’ after Golders Green attack here’s what he must do
News.content:
Jeer Starmer

AS BOOS rang out during Keir Starmer’s visit to Golders Green yesterday, one of the victims will have left him in no doubt where many Jewish people believe the blame lies.

“I definitely feel the Government has let us down,” said Shilome Rand.



“The streets of London are not safe for Jewish people.”



Ministers suddenly chucking another £25million for added security yesterday won’t do anything to solve the root cause.

It’s the shamefully spineless response of police and Government to hate peddled every week by pro-Palestinian fanatics which has allowed Islamist extremism to flourish.

The consequences of not cracking down on the “Globalise the Intifada” hate mob can now be seen in their sinister takeover of the Green Party.

The PM’s statement yesterday offered no concrete plans to tackle any of this.

Trump card

The King’s importance to British interests cannot be overstated.



Black arts

News.title: Hilarious moment Trump says wearing bulletproof vest would make him look too fat after assassination attempt
News.content:
DONALD Trump has hilariously quipped that donning a bulletproof vest would make him look too fat after the recent botched murder plot.

The US president was the prime target of would-be-assassin Cole Thomas Allen, who allegedly stormed the White House Correspondents’ Dinner armed to the teeth on Saturday.





But Trump appears to be unphased by the terrifying attempt on his life, instead joking with reporters: “I don’t know if I could handle looking 20 pounds heavier,” when asked if he would now wear a bulletproof vest.

The gag was met with roars of laughter in the Oval Office, as Trump added: “Some of these guys are physical specimens…” before being drowned out by more guffaws from the room.

The president was taking media questions while signing a series of executive orders after bidding an emotional farewell to King Charles and Queen Camilla.

He announced a shock removal of US tariffs on Scottish whiskey in honour of the royal couple, which was met with delight from British Business Secretary Peter Kay.



But Trump’s week could have looked very different had his brave Secret Service agents not prevented Allen from entering the Washington Hilton ballroom last Saturday.

A chilling selfie was released by prosecutors showing the suspected gunman heavily armed in his hotel room ahead of the alleged shooting.



In it, the suspect wears black pants, a black shirt, and a bright red tie, and his full arsenal of deadly weapons can be seen.

He has a shotgun slung over one shoulder with a handgun in a shoulder holster, a hunting knife sheathed at his chest, and an ammunition bag.

He also had wire cutters, pliers, and multiple more knives on him when he was arrested, cops said.



Prosecutors said he took the mirror selfie in full evening wear just minutes before he charged the dinner with several Trump administration officials in attendance alongside members of the media.

Allen was later charged with trying to assassinate Trump.

US Attorney Jeanine Pirro confirmed the 31-year-old was also facing firearms and assault charges.

Trump and Melania were rushed out of the dinner after a gunman opened fire.

Guests at the event were forced to hide under tables as Secret Service agents filled the room after Allen allegedly charged a security checkpoint.



Only one law enforcement officer was injured in the ordeal – after his phone miraculously deflected a bullet.

Erika Kirk, whose husband Charlie Kirk was assassinated months prior, attended the event and was left visibly shaken and sobbing as she was escorted out of the venue saying, “I just want to go home.”

Trump shared a video on Truth Social after the incident, appearing to show the suspect quickly run past security where two Secret Service agents can then be seen pulling out their guns.

At a press conference afterwards, Trump said the suspect, whom he called a “would-be assassin,” was armed with several weapons and was wearing a bulletproof vest.

“It’s always shocking when something like this happens,” Trump said.



“The fact that we were sitting next to each other, the First Lady on my right, and I heard a noise.”

The president added that at first, he thought the noise was a tray being dropped by a staff member at the event.

He revealed Melania was the first to raise suspicion that the sound could have been from gunfire.

Allen allegedly wrote a manifesto detailing his plans to “fix” the world.

He called himself the “Friendly Federal Assassin,” and wrote to his family and friends that he did not expect forgiveness.



“I apologize to everyone….who suffered before I was able to attempt this, to all who may still suffer after, regardless of my success or failure,” he allegedly wrote.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Allen’s brother was the one to alert police about his writings.

US officials have said that the “evidence of his guilt is overwhelming,” and that Allen faces a possible sentence of life in prison if convicted.

News.title: Evil Scots mum ‘paid tribute’ to baby she murdered by pampering herself with beauty treatments days after tot’s death
News.content:
A MONSTER mum told how she paid “tribute” to her newborn baby by pampering herself with beauty treatments just days after she murdered her.

Sick Nicole Blain, 30, revealed she went for tanning sessions and got her nails done after fatally battering 19-day-old tot Thea and fumed: “I was choking for a sunbed.”





She inflicted “car crash” injuries on the helpless infant including three skull fractures, brain damage and broken ribs then tried to blame a toddler for the killing.

Blain went through her self-care routing while protesting her innocence in a series of bizarre now-deleted TikToks posted in the hours after she took the infant’s life and even traded messages with a bereaved parent.

In one vid, she said: “I was pregnant for nine months — I was choking for a sunbed.

“The nails I got were inspired by Thea.

Most read in The Scottish Sun SHAMELESS Monster mum bleats about baby she murdered as she pleads for funeral donations



“I have been for two sunbeds.

“My eyelashes I did myself.



“It made me feel better for five minutes then I feel bad for doing all these things.

“If anybody has any questions about how my daughter passed then come to me, her mother, and I will tell you.

“Simple.”

Blain began uploaded videos to TikTok days after she killed Thea — including one four-minute clip in which she describes her beauty routine.

She lies in bed wrapped in a fluffy bathrobe as she flashes her fingers tipped with sparkly purple nails.



The murderer claims she was told to get the treatments under “doctors’ orders” so she would “feel a wee bit normal”.

In another she begs for cash donations for the girl’s funeral, pleading “I want a horse and carriage, that takes a wee bit of money”.

And she nuzzles her clothing and a stuffed lamb toy in others.

In a 13-second video, she is seen lying on top of a pink knitted blanket and matching teddies claiming she was “sleeping with Thea’s stuff to go in her coffin”.

The killer was offered support by a mum who revealed she lost her baby on the streaming website and offered to chat privately.



She responded with a love heart emoji and said: “It’s the worst pain a parent can go through, I hope I find the strength you have.”

Blain was found guilty on Wednesday after causing 19-day-old Thea Wilson “catastrophic” injuries in July 2023.

Evidence from various medics showed she shook the girl’s tiny body and repeatedly smacked her head off a hard surface to fracture her skull – despite Blain claiming another child had injured the tot.

Her lies were dismissed as “nonsense” and she was found guilty after week-long trial at the High Court in Glasgow.

In court Blain cried and sobbed hysterically after hearing the verdict.



Jurors had sat through hours of disturbing evidence and heard tiny Thea had suffered “car crash” injuries including whiplash, at the hands of Blain.

The tot suffered three skull fractures, bleeding in her eyes, brain damage, a bleed in her spinal canal and two broken ribs after the attack on July 14, 2023 at her flat in Greenock, Inverclyde.

Blain lied that a two-year-old had accidentally dropped the baby causing the injuries, even telling a social worker: “I don’t know how I will forgive (the child).”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But various medics gave evidence saying it was “very, very unlikely a toddler would be capable of inflicting those injuries”.

Lord Scott warned Blain she would be receiving a life sentence when she returns for sentencing later this month (May).

News.title: Welcome to UK’s most shoplifted street where druggies ransack shops, shove salami down pants & attack with syringes
News.content:
IT’S 7am on a quiet street in Gateshead and a shoplifter legs it out of a store carrying a basket piled high with washing pods, floor cleaner and coffee.

It is just the start of another day of pilfering on a shopping street less than a quarter of a mile long where store owners have logged 260 thefts in just two months.





Welcome to Britain’s most shoplifted street, where gangs are so brazen they simply saunter into stores, take what they want and stroll out.

The main road in the Wrekenton area of Gateshead is targeted by a rabble of up to 30 drug addicts who are in and out of jail while repeatedly robbing the same shops, primarily for easily sellable meat and toiletries.

Store staff are too frightened — and powerless — to stop the offenders. Police constantly arrest them but shop owners told us that “soft” magistrates just give them a slap on the wrist, after being regaled with stories of childhood trauma and addiction.

Shop staff in Wrekenton have been threatened with knives, ammonia and dirty needles that thieves claim are infected with hepatitis.





One Lidl worker told us: “When I see them come into our shop I start shaking because I know they’re going to try to run out with booze, and they are violent if confronted.

“It happens up to five times a day. It’s terrifying at night when you are the only one on the till. They target high-value stuff like steak and booze.”

Only one store owner on Wrekenton’s main street is fighting back, admitting to altercations with the robbers. Sanjiv Johal said: “If they steal from me and I have to take them outside there’s only ever one winner.”

Same faces over and over

When The Sun visited the UK’s Ground Zero for shoplifting this week, thieves were already at it by 10am. One swiped bottles of gin from a shelf at a major supermarket and scarpered.

Throughout the day, we watched the usual suspects standing around ­smoking large cannabis joints before dipping in and out of shops.

The crooks included a dad with a pram and another man on crutches.

We watched as they arrived in store. They yelled at each other, rowed and, in one instance, argued with a young staff member.

They seemed determined to attract attention, but it seemed to be a ploy to distract shop staff — as one of the men would slip away from the main group amid the chaos.

By lunchtime, they appeared to be so inebriated they could barely stand. Store managers say that sunny days can attract more than 30 gang members who congregate on benches, sometimes blasting out music.

There are eight shops on Wrekenton’s main drag that the gang target, as the others are hairdressers, takeaways, a bookmaker, and a vape shop which keeps its wares behind the till.



Five of the eight stores are members of a Shopwatch group on WhatsApp, set up eight weeks ago. It has already recorded 260 thefts. It is a staggering figure if you consider last year’s “hotspot” street, Central Avenue in West Bridgford, Notts, recorded 140 thefts over 12 months.

The grim reality is that store managers and police in places like Wrekenton know exactly who is robbing them as it is the same faces over and over again.

And it is no wonder the thieves ­operate with impunity when you ­consider the punishment.

The Sun revealed this week how cops in some towns give up on 90 per cent of shoplifting cases within weeks.

When I see them come into our shop I start shaking because I know they’re going to try to run out with booze, and they are violent if confronted Lidl worker

Northumbria Police, which covers Gateshead, saw 12,723 offences between March 2025 and February this year. Figures show that 8,095 went unsolved, and police closed 6,030 of those cases within a month.

The North East is ranked as the number one region for shoplifting in England and Wales, with 11.8 reported crimes per 1,000 people.

Just one in five offences led to a charge or court summons, according to the Centre For Social Justice. Their research also shows that the number of offences committed by individual thieves has near-doubled since the pandemic, from 5.5 to 9.1 thefts per convicted shoplifter.

It reflects a national picture of repeat thefts after The Sun revealed in January how shoplifters strike three times every minute across the UK.

In Wrekenton, there seems to be no end to the misery.

One shop owner, who was too scared to be named, told us: “A big part of the issue around here is drugs.



“Also, a lot of the matriarchs who kept family values are dead now so there’s nobody to rein these people in.

“I’ve had a few addicts live in the flats above the shop and they are a mess. As soon as they are back from court or prison, they’re back to thieving again. They were eating out of the bins at the back of the Spar shop a few months ago — it’s disgusting.

“I used to have lots of empathy for addicts but it’s run out now.

“They get the offer of help but don’t take it. Big shops can absorb the loss but not us smaller owners.”

Wrekenton, four miles from Newcastle city centre, has 6,000 residents and sits in the High Fell council ward, which is one of the poorest areas in England — 53 per cent of locals are rated the most deprived in the country, according to a Gateshead Council report.



You only have to look around to see how Wrekenton’s ­residents have been left behind.

Many middle-aged people need sticks or wheelchairs to get around, while in shops mums are seen counting pennies to pay for their shopping. It is heartbreaking but shop owners say poverty is no excuse for the gangs to rob.

You can see that store owner Sanjiv Johal is totally exasperated.

His discount shop, Poundzone, is stacked with bargains like a 24-case of Coke for a fiver, an industrial-sized pack of cleaning wipes for £3.50, and reed diffusers for £1.

Sanjiv, 39, told us: “We keep things as cheap as we can because we want to help people out. But it doesn’t make a bit of difference to the shoplifters.”

It would take a brave man to try to steal from Sanjiv, who has 31 CCTV cameras in his shop, and he is open about the fact he is willing to stand up for his business.

He said: “There’s been instances where staff have been threatened with knives, with dirty syringes, and a woman once came in carrying a bottle full of clear liquid, told us it was ammonia and that she was going to throw it in our faces.

“I’ve had a few altercations with some of the addicts who try to take from me and I’m not afraid of them. They know that as well.”

Sanjiv knows getting physical is a risk but it is one he is willing to take and claims local police, who we saw regularly patrolling the street in a squad car, have been supportive.

Violent robbery

In his shop window he has displayed a “wall of shame” of images, showing 49 faces of those he says are well-known shoplifters. He also gives the thieves nicknames like Methy Blinders and The Slob.



Among the thieves are locals with criminal convictions, including Tanya Tait, 44, Callum Little, 27, and Lee Robson, 46.

There’s been instances where staff have been threatened with knives, with dirty syringes Sanjiv Johal

In February, Tait was jailed for four years for her part in a violent robbery of an 81-year-old man in his home. She helped burglar Danny McGuire, 36, gain access to the OAP’s home because she knew him and the pair stole his safe with £300 inside.

Newcastle Crown Court heard how she also attacked a woman with multiple sclerosis, who was left suffering a bleed on the brain.

Callum Little was jailed for 36 weeks in February for a five-week shoplifting spree.

He was caught on CCTV stealing a display of Creme Eggs before dropping them. Robson has been described as a “prolific offender”, who was locked up for 11 months in 2023 for store thefts.

Sanjiv says courts are far too soft on the offenders, while shop assistants are lambasted for trying to stop the thieves.

Only last month, Waitrose sacked an employee of 17 years for stopping a shoplifter who had ransacked a display of Lindt Gold Bunny Easter eggs.

Walker Smith, 54, who was fired from the Clapham Junction branch in South London, said the alleged culprit was a “serial offender”.

Two Morrisons workers have also been sacked after failing to follow the company’s “deter, not detain” policy.

Store manager Sean Egan, 46, who worked for the supermarket chain for 29 years, was dismissed after he tried to thwart a repeat thief in Aldridge, near Walsall.



Jane Pilborough, 62, saw her 30-year career ended after what she described as a “tug of war” with a teen trying to walk off with a packet of chicken bites at Morrisons in Newark, Notts.

Locals in Gateshead say more must be done to tackle the raiders. Business owner Kelly Jepson, 52, said: “They just seem to do what they want. They walk in a shop then walk out with no punishment.”

Shop worker Dean Jackson, 37, described the crisis as being “out of control”, while local mortgage advisor Hayley Ward, 43, has also witnessed shoplifting up close.

They just seem to do what they want. They walk in a shop then walk out with no punishment Kelly Jepson, business owner

She said: “A few weeks ago I saw a man who had stuffed his trouser bottoms with loads of meat. He had everything from salami to beef.”

Labour has vowed to crack down on the shoplifting epidemic, scrapping a guideline that saw police ignore thieves who stole goods worth less than £200.

Whether it will have an impact on the addicts who congregate outside Sanjiv’s shop in Wrekenton is yet to be determined.

Meanwhile he, like shop workers up and down Britain, will remain on the frontline of an epidemic that continues to sweep the country.

News.title: Plymouth bomb to be detonated as Aldi evacuated and 'stay away' warning issued
News.content:
Plymouth bomb to be detonated as Aldi evacuated and 'stay away' warning issued

A 250kg German bomb is not safe to be removed from a neighbourhood in Plymouth, which means it will have to be detonated with people evacuated from the area in advance

View 3 Images A historic German SC250, which is a 250kg air-dropped bomb, was found in Plymouth (Image: Plymouth Live / BPM Media)

A World War II bomb which forced the evacuation of an Aldi in Plymouth cannot be removed - and will now be detonated.

‌



The Royal Navy confirmed the 250kg German bomb would not be safe to be transferred after it was uncovered at a building site in Southway.

‌



Large amounts of sand will be used to cover the bomb before it is blown up on Friday, to reduce the amount of shrapnel and fragments spread by the controlled explosion.

‌



A no-fly zone is in place for safety and people have also been urged to stay away from the area, with locals told there will be no visible view of the detonation.

View 3 Images A cordon in place in Southway (Image: Matt Gilley/FPS Images)

Met Office predicts 26C heat surge on Friday as maps show 38 counties to sizzle READ MORE :

More than 1,200 properties have been evacuated and more residents have also been urged to leave with alternative accommodation available at Southway Community Centre if needed.

‌



Speaking outside the centre this evening, Colonel Nick Handy told press: "A lot of people say well it’s been in the ground for 80 years, what's the problem with it?

"The simple reason is, the fuses are the thing that makes it go bang and we need to understand whether that's a time fuse with a mechanical timer or an electrical fuse that's got a capacitor that is drained and therefore safe. That dictates whether we actually move that item.

View 3 Images People have been evacuated from the area (Image: Shannon Brown/PlymouthLive)

‌



"Unfortunately we cannot get a definitive X-ray of the second fuse and therefore it's not safe to move that item. So we're going to blow it in situ.

"We’re going to try our hardest to deflagrate that item and burn it inside of a structure that will limit the damage to the local surroundings. I'm pretty confident that mitigation that we put up will limit most of the damage. But we'll look to do that at some point tomorrow.

"We’re going to work tirelessly through the night to ensure that that mitigation protects the buildings that face the times and indeed cover the items to ensure the least amount of blast and fragmentation come out from the area where we do our work."

‌



Plymouth City Council said: "Royal Navy and Army UXO specialists have now completed a rigorous and detailed assessment of the device. They have advised that it is not possible to safely remove it. The only safe option is to make the device safe in situ, which will involve a controlled detonation.

"Specialist teams are currently building a mitigation structure using large quantities of sand to reduce the potential impact of the detonation. The detonation will take place at some point tomorrow and will only take place once all safety measures are fully in place.

"Please note, you will not be able to see this ‘detonation’ from any point around the cordon, so please stay away from the area. The Police have also issued a no-fly zone over the site, which means no drones are allowed."

‌



Originally a 100m cordon was in place, which was then expanded to 200m as a precautionary measure - and then 400m, reported PlymouthLive.

At 7am today, Plymouth City Council said: "Royal Navy unexploded ordnance (UXO) specialists have worked through the night to continue their assessment of the device discovered in Southway and to determine the safest way to make it secure.

"Plymouth City Council is supporting this work by supplying large quantities of sand to help ensure the device remains stable while specialist operations continue.

Article continues below

"Meanwhile, work to evacuate approximately 1,260 households within the 400‑metre safety cordon is ongoing. Devon and Cornwall Police, supported by volunteers from a number of organisations e.g. Coast Guard, are continuing door‑to‑door visits to provide residents with information and encourage people to leave their homes for their own safety."

It has since been confirmed with the Royal Navy UXO experts that the device is a historic German SC250 - a 250kg air-dropped weapon.

News.title: Donald Trump's wild 24 hours with dementia test demand and very vain admission
News.content:
Donald Trump's wild 24 hours with dementia test demand and very vain admission

Everything that's happened in Trumpworld in the last 24 hours that you might have missed - including a curious moment of honesty in the Oval Office

View 3 Images (Image: AP)

Donald Trump has a habit of calling people he doesn't like "low IQ" people. But only some people.

‌



Today, he referred to Democrat minority leader Hakeem Jeffries by that particular slur, over his comments regarding a particularly troubling Supreme Court verdict, which you can read about below. Others who've been branded "low IQ" by Trump include Representative Maxine Waters, former Vice President Kamala Harris, Supreme Court Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson, Congresswomen Jasmine Crockett, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Ilhan Omar. Of the 20 or so people we've found who he's referred to as "Low IQ", just 7 of them are white. The website Truthout today found 8 in 10 of the Truth Social posts in which Trump referred to someone as "Low IQ" were targeting a person of colour. I only mention it because today he suggested Barack Obama should have had to take a "cognitive test" before he stood for President, and applauded a Supreme Court ruling that hollows out a 40-year-old law that prevented states from making it harder for black people to get elected.

‌



You may draw your own conclusions.

‌



Meanwhile in Trumpworld

Trump won't be wearing a bulletproof vest

He's considering pulling troops out of more European countries

He gave James Comey's lawyers a freebie

He thinks presidential candidates should have to take a dementia test

He fumed as his vaccine skeptic Surgeon General pick got torpedoed

And he replaced her with a Fox News contributor

Here's what you need to know

‌



1. Trump won't be wearing a bulletproof vest

Trump was asked if there were any changes planned for his personal security - particularly if he was going to start wearing a bulletproof vest.

Trump pooh poohed this idea, saying: "I don't know if I can handle looking 20 pounds heavier."

A rare moment of honesty.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

2. Trump threatens to pull troops out of Italy and Spain as well as Germany

Trump has been in a very public spat with Chancellor Friedrich Merz - after the German leader said the US was being "humiliated" in the Iran war. In response, Trump has been threatening to pull US troops out of Germany - which would have serious security implications for Europe. Well, today a very grumpy looking Donald Trump was asked in the Oval Office whether he was going to do the same with Italy and Spain, after they were less than cooperative in the conflict. "Yeah, probably," he said. "Why shouldn't I? Italy has not been of any help to us, and Spain has been horrible."

3. Trump gives James Comey's defence lawyers a freebie

Ex-FBI Director and Trump nemesis James Comey's defence lawyers are expected to argue against the nonsense indictment against him on "vindictive prosecution". And they probably won't have much trouble making that stick. The indictment relates to was a photo of a beach with "86 47" written using seashells, which Comey posted on Instagram last year. The FBI and Justice Department claim that "86" in this context didn't just mean "remove or expel", as most people understand it, but actually to kill, something Comey has always denied. It's the second time Trump's Justice Department has tried to indict Comey, after similarly frivolous charges of lying to congress crashed and burned last year.

‌



View 3 Images The post that Comey has been indicted over (Image: comey/Instagram)

And as if it weren't transparent enough that this was a case of judicial harassment, Trump keeps posting things like this on Truth Social: ""86" is a mob term for "kill him." They say 86 him! 86 47 means "kill President Trump. James Comey, who is a Dirty Cop, one of the worst, knows this full well! EIGHT MILES OUT, SIX FEET DOWN! Didn't he also lie to the FBI about this??? I think so! President DJT"

For the record, Trump is wrong on this. The term "86" is not widely used in mob-talk, in the movies or in real life. In fact, ABC News did a search of scripts from the American Film Institute's top 10 gangster films, which found no trace of the phrase being used. It's possible Trump is getting it confused with "deep six", which is a common mob trope, meaning to destroy or dispose of something irretrievably. But even that isn't usually used as slang for murder.

‌



4. Trump demands people running for President take "cognitive tests"

Also in Trump's flurry of Truth Social posts this afternoon was this absolute gem. "Anybody running for President or Vice President should be forced to take a Cognitive Examination prior to entering the Race!" He went on to brag that he'd taken the test "three times during my ("THREE!") Terms as President, and ACED IT ALL THREE TIMES -- An Achievement that, even on a single Exam, according to the Doctors, has rarely been done before!"

What he didn't mention - and what his doctors apparently didn't have the heart to tell him - is that the "cognitive test" his doctors keep giving him - which from how he's described it is the Montreal Cognitive Assessment is most frequently used to check for early signs of dementia in the elderly. It stands to reason that Trump, being the most elderly President of all time, would be asked to take the test from time to time.

He also claimed: "By doing so, we wouldn't be surprised at people like Barack "Hussein" Obama, or Sleepy Joe Biden, getting "ELECTED." Our Country would be a much better place!" I'm not sure which bit of this is my favourite, the suggestion that Barack Obama, a man who was in his late 40s when elected, might have been at risk of dementia, or the quotes around "ELECTED".

‌



View 3 Images Donald Trump was the oldest person ever to take the oath of office (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

5. Trump fumes as "MAHA" surgeon general pick gets torpedoed

Trump fumed on Truth Social after he was forced to pull his pick for Surgeon General - Casey Means - after her confirmation stalled in the Senate. Means, a dietitian, wellness influencer and darling of RFK JR's rampantly anti-science "MAHA" movement, had hit the rocks in the process, in part, because she stopped short of recommending vaccines against measles and influenza in her confirmation hearings. Trump lashed out at Bill Cassidy, who chairs the Senate Health Committee.

He wrote: "For months, Senator Bill Cassidy (of the GREAT State of Louisiana!), a very disloyal person whose "TRUMP" Endorsement got him elected, but later voted to impeach "President Trump" on what has now proven to be a total Hoax and Scam, has stood in the way of Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s Nominee, Casey Means, for the important position of U.S. Surgeon General. I nominated Casey, a strong MAHA Warrior, at the recommendation of Secretary Kennedy, who understands the MAHA Movement better than anyone, with perhaps the possible exception of ME! Nevertheless, despite Senator Cassidy's intransigence and political games, Casey will continue to fight for MAHA on the many important Health issues facing our Country, such as the rising childhood disease epidemic, increased autism rates, poor nutrition, over-medicalization, and researching the root causes of infertility, and many other difficult medical problems. Casey, thank you for your service to our Nation! President DONALD J. TRUMP" He went on: "Hopefully all of the Great Republican People of Louisiana, which I won, BIG, three times, will be voting Bill Cassidy OUT OF OFFICE in the upcoming Republican Primary! President DONALD J. TRUMP"

‌



6. He replaces her with a Fox News contributor

Because of course he does.

Moments after pulling Means' nomination, Trump wrote: "I am pleased to announce that I am nominating Dr. Nicole B. Saphier to be the next SURGEON GENERAL OF THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA. Nicole is a STAR physician who has spent her career guiding women facing breast cancer through their diagnosis and treatment while tirelessly advocating to increase early cancer detection and prevention, while at the same time working with men and women on all other forms of cancer diagnoses and treatments. She is also an INCREDIBLE COMMUNICATOR, who makes complicated health issues more easily understood by all Americans." That "INCREDIBLE" communication is done, for the most part, on Fox News, where she's signed up as a contributor.

7. Slow clap for the Supreme Court for winding back 40 years of progress on racism in politics

The Supreme Court did a bad thing yesterday, and it takes a bit of explaining, but it's important. So back in 1965 President Lyndon Johnson signed the Voting Rights Act (VRA) into law - which said states aren't allowed to discriminate on the basis of race when it comes to elections. One of the reasons it was introduced was to prevent racist state governments from redrawing constituency boundaries to slice up areas where a lot of black people live - something that was happening at the time, and which made it incredibly difficult for people of colour to get elected to Congress. This, they called 'racial gerrymandering'. The VRA gave courts the power to strike down maps like this, crucially, without having to prove a state intended to discriminate - only that the result was discriminatory.

‌



Fast forward to today, and a row over Louisiana's voting map. The state drew a map that civil rights groups challenged under the VRA, saying it diluted the voting power of black people in the state. The courts agreed, and told the State to re-draw the map and add a second black-majority district in Louisiana. Then it got confusing, because that second map was then challenged by Republicans, who argued that adding a district because of race was, itself, unconstitutional. This made it all the way to the Supreme Court yesterday - and the conservative 6-3 majority on the court decided the second map was unconstitutional. But that doesn't just affect the Louisiana map, it re-writes the legal test for the VRA. The court basically ruled that a map is only illegal if you can prove the state intended to discriminate. This effectively hollows out the Voting Rights Act and makes it much harder to challenge ropey attempts to lock minorities out of politics.

Now let's all sit back and watch Republicans in Southern states redraw their maps just in time for 2028.

8. Trump is obviously delighted

Trump was tickled pink when the decision was revealed to him in the Oval Office yesterday. And since then he's been crowing about it on Truth Social. "Today's 6-3 Supreme Court decision in the Callais case is a BIG WIN for Equal Protection under the Law, as it returns the Voting Rights Act to its Original Intent, which was to protect against intentional Racial Discrimination," he wrote. "Thank you to brilliant Justice Samuel Alito for authoring this important and appropriate Opinion. Congratulations! President DONALD J. TRUMP"

News.title: Donald Trump praises Queen Camilla during ceremonial White House farewell
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Donald Trump praises Queen Camilla during ceremonial White House farewell

As the King and Queen have bid farewell to the President and First Lady, Trump was quick to compliment Camilla to the monarch as she had her back turned

View 4 Images Donald Trump and Queen Camilla in Washington DC today (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

King Charles and Queen Camilla have bid farewell to the President and First Lady of the United States in a ceremony outside the White House.

‌



After completing a day of engagements in New York on Wednesday, Their Majesties travelled back to Washington DC to say goodbye to Donald and Melania Trump after their several days together.

‌



As the Trumps greeted the King and Queen as they arrived by car on the South Portico of the nation’s capital, the US leader and the monarch exchanged pleasantries and compliments before they headed inside the White House to formally bring a close to their visit.

‌



Meghan Markle breaks silence on divisive trip to Australia READ MORE :

View 4 Images Charles and Camilla bid farewell to the President and First Lady of the United States (Image: Will Oliver/UPI/Shutterstock)

And as lip reader Jeremy Freeman told the Mirror, President Trump was full of praise for Queen Camilla. As the two couples stood outside the White House, Trump said to the King: “It’s been good. It’s been important. Look at everybody,” before pointing to Camilla and saying: “I don’t know how she does it, she’s amazing”.

The President then turned to the Queen and said: “It was fantastic. I look forward to seeing you again. Thank you for making it a success. Love to the grandchildren”.

‌



First Lady Melania also thanked the royal couple for their visit, as she said to Camilla: “I’m glad you had a great time,” before turning to Charles and saying: “Thank you, we loved having you here. See you soon. We loved you. Have a good journey.”

View 4 Images The King and President Trump exchanged fond farewells (Image: AP)

Melania also noticed that Camilla was wearing the Tiffany brooch that she was given as a gift by the First Lady during their trip to the UK last September, as she said: “Oh that’s so wonderful.”

‌



As Their Majesties, the President and the First Lady posed for photos outside the White House, they were called upon by reporters as one asked the King: “Your Majesty, what do you think of the Trump renaissance and all the improvements in DC?" Charles responded: "I like it, very interesting."

Charles and Camilla drove away to attend their day of engagements in Virginia, as Trump continues to sing their praises to the onlooking media. The US president hailed Charles as “the greatest king in my book”, adding that he and Camilla are “really great people. We need more people like that in our country.”

View 4 Images Trump complimented Camilla as Their Majesties departed Washington DC (Image: Aaron Schwartz/UPI/Shutterstock)

‌



After the King and Queen departed Washington DC, they headed to Arlington in Virginia where they placed a wreath on the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at the Arlington National Cemetery, and received a 21 gun salute.

Their Majesties then travelled to the small town of Front Royal, where they attended a ‘block party’: a neighbourhood celebration to celebrate America’s 250th ‘birthday’.

Article continues below

As a parade of marching bands, cheerleaders, the town’s local community trolley and classic British and American cars proceeds down Main Street, The King and Queen, accompanied by the Governor of Virginia, Ms. Abigail Spanberger and the Mayor of Front Royal Ms. Lori Athey Cockrell, joined in the bustling community celebration.

News.title: British airport is closing forever in 2026 as all flights will stop within days
News.content:
British airport is closing forever in 2026 as all flights will stop within days

Coventry Airport will cease operations on June 11 and the last planes will be leaving on May 9 - it has been running for 90 years and will be replaced by a green energy site

View 4 Images Coventry Airport is closing down this year (Image: Wikimedia Commons)

An airport will see its last flight take off next month after 90 years - and will be replaced by a multi-million pound battery site making green energy.

‌



The UK Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) confirmed Coventry Airport will cease operations on June 11 and the last planes will be leaving before that on May 9.

‌



The airport is steeped in history having originally been called Baginton Aerodrome when it opened in 1936 and operated as an RAF base during World War II. The decision to close comes with the airport not operating scheduled passenger flights, as it is mainly used for charter flights or training.

‌



View 4 Images The airport will cease operations on June 11 (Image: Wikimedia Commons)

High cholesterol symptoms includes 'smelly' warning sign READ MORE :

Keir Starmer heckled by protestors on visit to Golders Green to meet emergency services READ MORE :

A spokesperson from the CAA said: "Coventry Aerodrome has given formal notice to us of its plan to close the airport permanently with effect from 11 June 2026."

The land is slated for demolition to pave the way for Greenpower Park, a large-scale battery production plant, or “gigafactory,” intended to support the UK’s shift toward electric vehicles.

‌



Speaking about the airport's notice to the CAA, the Rigby Group statement said: "This procedural submission, first envisaged when local planning approval for Green Power Park was granted in 2022, enables the next phase of infrastructure work for the site to proceed."

View 4 Images An Air Atlantique DC3 Dakota at Coventry Airport in 1985 (Image: Mirrorpix)

Jim O'Boyle, the councillor responsible for jobs and regeneration at Coventry City Council, said: "What we want to see are thousands of jobs created here, giving the area an economic lift."

‌



Over the past decades, it has handled freight, light aircraft, and occasional commercial flights. During the 1980s Hards Travel flew travellers to Spain, France, Italy and Austria as part of package holidays.

In 2004, Thomsonfly began flights to popular destinations such as Palma, Valencia, Rome, Nice, Marseille, Naples, Pisa, Venice, and Jersey. Wizz Air also flew passengers to Gdańsk and Katowice, reported the Express.

View 4 Images Pope John Paul II's visit to Coventry Airport in 1982 (Image: Mirrorpix)

Article continues below

However on September 1 2008, Wizz Air confirmed it would not continue its seasonal service from Coventry to Gdańsk and Katowice. In a further setback for the airport, Thomsonfly confirmed on October 15 2008 that it would cease operations at Coventry Airport, citing a shift in focus toward charter services following its merger with First Choice Airways.

Coventry Airport also played host to a Papal visit in 1982, when Pope John Paul II toured the UK and drew an estimated 350,000 people to the site.

In May 2009, Coventry Airport was put up for sale and Sir Peter Rigby's Rigby Group took over ownership on April 28 2010. It fully reopened later that year.

News.title: Adventure holidays UK: Brits swapping relaxed breaks for active adventure travel
News.content:
Adventure holidays UK: Brits swapping relaxed breaks for active adventure travel

A new generation of travellers are embracing 'maxx-packing' - the art of fitting in as many adventurous experiences into a holiday as possible, with over half of Brits now considering themselves active holidaymakers

View 3 Images Holidaymakers are cramming as many experiences as possible into their trips (Image: Getty Images)

British holidaymakers are getting to grips with maxx-packing — the art of cramming as many thrilling experiences as possible into a single trip.

‌



Traditionally, many of us have viewed holidays as a chance to unwind and recharge, with the occasional spot of leisurely sightseeing thrown in for good measure.

‌



But a new breed of traveller is rising at the crack of dawn to squeeze every last drop out of each day — and gruelling activities are firmly on the agenda.

‌



More than half (53%) of Brits consider themselves a maxx-packer, with just 31% saying they prefer a relaxing holiday to an active one, according to research by Tourism New Zealand.

Met Office predicts 26C heat surge on Friday as maps show 38 counties to sizzle READ MORE :

View 3 Images Travellers are getting up at dawn to get the most out of their holidays (Image: BirminghamLive)

As many as two-thirds (63%) say they are no longer content lounging on a sun-bed for the entirety of their break — and 60% are more inclined to lace up their trainers for a run or hike than have a lie-in while on holiday.

‌



Demand for action-packed trips has rocketed over the past decade. While just 13% had embarked on their first maxx-packing holiday before 2015, nine in ten had experienced this style of break by 2025.

The trend is even more striking amongst younger travellers, with 40% stating they opt for active holidays as they provide a chance to disconnect from social media.

Dedicated members of this emerging holiday movement can clock up an average of 12km of running, 14km of cycling, and 8km of swimming over the course of a one-week trip.

‌



Research also revealed that a maxx-packing holiday can prove nearly as demanding as the activities themselves, with 53% identifying one specific obstacle as planning.

To overcome this barrier, 100% Pure New Zealand has teamed up with Flight Centre to launch the Maxx Package, a 12-day customisable, self-drive adventure packed with thrilling outdoor experiences across the country's stunning natural scenery.

The journey travels from the North to the South Island, taking in five remarkable destinations to guarantee travellers can make the most of every single moment.

‌



Key experiences include a helicopter flight over Franz Josef Glacier, trekking the Tongariro Alpine Crossing and exploring the Lord of the Rings' Hobbiton.

View 3 Images The Lord of the Rings set is part of a new maxxpacking tour (Image: Handout)

The itinerary includes a stop at adventure capital Queenstown where jet boat excursions, bungee jumping, and lakeside strolls await, while in Hamilton, visitors can experience black water rafting through glow-worm-lit caves.

‌



René de Monchy, chief executive of 100% Pure New Zealand, said: "Adventure travel is part of New Zealand's heritage, it's in our DNA.

"Filled with immersive, invigorating experiences that draw manuhiri (visitors) into epic landscapes through movement – leaving you feeling rewarded and uplifted."

'Whether pursuing personal growth, a break from life's distractions, or you're someone who simply can't sit still, New Zealand provides it all – leaving travellers richer in stories they'll carry long after they return home.

Article continues below

"If you're not a maxx-packer there's plenty of sun-soaked beaches, breath-taking relaxation spots and delicious food and wine to tempt all kinds of travellers to the North and South Islands. New Zealand really is a destination for everyone".

Kelly Darke, travel agent at Flight Centre says: "The way people research and book trips has completely shifted - travellers want to come home with stories, not just a tan.

"The conversations we're having are less about destinations and more about doing them justice, making sure every day counts. That's driven by a growing expectation that every pound and moment spent on a holiday should deliver something exceptional, not just something restful." For further details and to arrange the maxx-packing itinerary, visit your local Flight Centre.

News.title: Donald Trump threatens to pull troops out of more countries in another blow to NATO
News.content:
Donald Trump threatens to pull troops out of more countries in another blow to NATO

The US President has already threatened to take US troops out of Germany as he feuds with Chancellor Friedrich Merz - and asked whether he'd do the same in Italy and Spain he said "probably, why shouldn't I?"

View Image Tump said: "Why shouldn't I?" (Image: AP)

Donald Trump threatened to pull troops out of more European countries in a fresh blow to NATO.

‌



It comes after he made a similar threat to withdraw from Germany.

‌



On his Truth Social website on Wednesday, Trump wrote that the US was reviewing possible troop reductions in Germany, with a “determination” to be made soon.

‌



And today he lashed out at Chancellor Friedrich Merz, telling Germany's leader he should “spend more time on ending the war with Russia / Ukraine ” and “fixing his broken Country” than concerning himself with Iran.

Merz said in comments this week that the US was being “humiliated” by Tehran in negotiations to end the Iran war.

And today, Trump was asked if he was also thinking about pulling troops out of Italy and Spain, in retaliation for their reluctance to get involved with the Iran war.

‌



"Yeah, probably," he said. "Why shouldn't I? Italy has not been of any help to us, and Spain has been horrible."

American allies in NATO have braced for a US troop withdrawal since just after the Trump administration took office, with Washington warning Europe would have to look after its own security, and that of Ukraine, in the future.

Depending on operations, exercises and troop rotations, around 80,000-100,000 US personnel are usually stationed in Europe. NATO allies have expected for more than a year that US troops deployed after Russia launched its all-out war on Ukraine in February 2022 would be first to leave.

‌



Germany hosts several US military facilities, including the headquarters of its European and Africa commands, Ramstein Air Base and a medical center in Landstuhl, where casualties from wars in places like Afghanistan and Iraq were treated. US nuclear missiles are also stationed in the country.

Ed Arnold, an expert in European security at the Royal United Services Institute, or RUSI, in London, said that the US gets a lot out of its presence in Germany — like logistics and support for Middle East combat operations — and was unlikely to withdraw.

Nico Lange from the Center of European Policy Analysis agreed, and said that there are approximately 36,000 US soldiers in Germany who primarily serve US interests, including “the projection of American power globally,” rather than helping with the defense of Germany.

Article continues below

The US has invested “substantial funds” in high-quality infrastructure in Germany that can't be moved overnight, and a different deployment would cost Washington a huge amount of money, which would require Trump to get approval from US Congress, Lange said.

As early as 2020, Trump announced plans to withdraw 11,900 US troops from Germany, but that didn't happen partly because US Congress didn't provide the necessary funds and a withdrawal would have required enormous investments elsewhere.

News.title: Cost-of-living crisis drives Brits to choose micro-treats over big purchases
News.content:
Cost-of-living crisis drives Brits to choose micro-treats over big purchases

Research suggests a third of us are too busy to take a break or switch off properly during the day, despite most saying playful moments are important for wellbeing – sparking a rise in small daily indulgences

View 2 Images Ice lollies are among the micro-treats Brits are turning to to get them through tough times (Image: Getty)

Brits are increasingly relying on small indulgences like ice lollies to help them cope as the cost-of-living squeeze tightens its grip.

‌



Fresh research has shown 35% of us are too stretched to properly take a break or genuinely unwind during the day, despite 79% acknowledging that moments of fun are crucial for mental health.

‌



When questioned about what lifts their spirits most, affordable pleasures like a small treat (21%) and time spent outdoors (21%) topped the rankings, according to the poll by Rowntree's.

‌



And while experiences, self-care and personal rewards remain valued, many Britons are prioritising financial caution over extravagance.

Price of your weekly food shop could FALL as Rachel Reeves suspends tariffs READ MORE :

3million UK households going without food in cost of living crisis READ MORE :

View 2 Images Many Brits are postponing home improvement projects amid the cost of living crisis (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Over half (54%) of Brits reported worries about living costs and 27% were postponing major expenditures such as vehicles or house improvements, according to recent findings.

Instead, three quarters of us are opting for swift and budget-friendly mood-boosters to add some brightness to the day, which explains why Rowntree's has launched two fresh ice-lolly varieties, perfectly timed with the arrival of spring sunshine.

Rowntree's Fruit Explosion, a contemporary twist on the traditional ice lolly, boasts dual-flavoured sorbet layers with a fruit sauce core, offering fans either apple and cherry sorbet with sour sauce or kiwi, mango and passion fruit sorbet with kiwi sauce.

Article continues below

Meanwhile, Rowntree's Fruit Pastilles Berries, drawing inspiration from the beloved classic, reimagines the legendary sweet as a cooling ice lolly.

A Rowntree's spokesperson commented: "It's still so important to take a moment for yourself, even if it's just something small. This is all about embracing little pauses in the day - a simple way to enjoy a bit of fun and bring a smile, no matter how busy life gets."

News.title: Jeffrey Epstein 'wrote secret prison suicide note' with haunting 4-word message
News.content:
Jeffrey Epstein 'wrote secret prison suicide note' with haunting 4-word message

A letter reportedly written by Jeffrey Epstein in jail before he died has been revealed after being kept for seven years in a New York courthouse vault

View 2 Images Epstein died in jail in 2019 (Image: Kypros)

A suicide note written by Jeffrey Epstein in jail has reportedly been kept secret for nearly seven years.

The disgraced financier's letter is said to have been locked up in a New York courthouse vault.

A cellmate said he discovered the note in July 2019, after Epstein was found unresponsive with a strip of cloth around his neck. Epstein survived that incident but weeks later was found dead in the jail.

On Thursday, The New York Times petitioned the judge to unseal the note which said it was “time to say goodbye”, cellmate Nicholas Tartaglione claimed. The note had been sealed by a federal judge as part of the cellmate’s own criminal case, according to documents and interviews.

View 2 Images Epstein died in his prison cell (Image: 60 Minutes/CBS)

High cholesterol symptoms includes 'smelly' warning sign READ MORE :

Met Office predicts 26C heat surge on Friday as maps show 38 counties to sizzle READ MORE :

And it meant that detectives investigating Epstein’s high-profile death lacked what could have been a key piece of evidence. A two-page document in the records reportedly describes how the scrawled message became tangled up in Tartaglione’s legal case.

It was said that Tartaglione’s lawyers authenticated the note, though there is no explanation of how this was done.

Tartaglione did mention the note on a podcast last year but the contents of the message were never revealed, despite so many calls for transparency over the investigation. Since December, the Justice Department has released millions of pages of documents related to Epstein.

Tartaglione, a former police officer, is behind bars serving four consecutive life sentences for murdering four people. Prison records show that a week after Epstein accused his cellmate of attacking him in July 2019, he later U-turned and said they “never had any issues”.

A Justice Department spokeswoman told the New York Times that the agency had not seen it and that the agency “underwent an exhaustive effort to collect all records in its possession,” including those from the Bureau of Prisons and the Office of the Inspector General.

Tartaglione said he found the note tucked into a graphic novel after Epstein was moved into a different part of the jail. The note is alleged to have said investigators “found nothing” from their investigations into the sex offender, Tartaglione recalled.

He said the message read: “What do you want me to do, bust out crying? Time to say goodbye.”

Article continues below

Epstein was found dead in his cell at a federal jail in Manhattan, New York, in August 2019 while he awaited trial on sex trafficking charges. His death was ruled as a suicide.

President Donald Trump’s assertion Thursday that the United States needs more people like King Charles III and Queen Camilla garnered mixed reactions from people, some who saw it as a dog whistle for his preferred type of immigrants, and others who saw it as an ironic joke given U.S.-U.K. history.

As Charles and Camilla departed from the White House on the fourth day of their U.S. visit, the president praised the Royal family members.

“Great people,” Trump began as the car carrying the King and Queen drove away.

“We need more people like that in our country,” he added, putting his hand to his mouth as though he was making an aside comment.

Some people pointed out the irony of desiring a King and Queen in the U.S., given America broke from Great Britain 250 years ago and established itself as a republic.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump called King Charles an ‘extraordinary man’ and said the United States could use more people like him and Queen Camilla ( Getty )

“We for sure could use more kings and queens of England here in the U.S.,” Jeff Timmer, a senior adviser to The Lincoln Project, an anti-Trump PAC, wrote.

“Ridiculous,” Grace Chong, the CFO/COO of former Trump ally Steve Bannon’s show, wrote.

Others interpreted the president’s comments to be a thinly veiled attempt at stating his preference for a specific type of immigrant.

“White Anglo Saxon Protestants,” lawyer and legal analyst Jeffrey Evan Gold wrote.

“White people? Doesn’t even try and be discreet,” another X user said.

The president has used similar statements that vaguely refer to a group of people to describe his preference or support for something without directly saying it.

“Why can’t we have some people from Norway, Sweden?” Trump asked during a rally last year, while complaining that the U.S. allows “people from s***hole countries.” He listed Afghanistan, Haiti and Somalia as examples of “hellholes.”

open image in gallery The White House posted online calling King Charles III and President Donald Trump ‘two Kings’ ( Reuters )

The administration has restricted immigration from Afghanistan, Haiti, Somalia, Syria and other African and Middle Eastern countries. In addition to placing a full ban on at least 19 countries, the administration has also sought to reduce the number of refugees from Haiti and Syria.

Yet, Trump has expanded access for white South Africans, who the president says are facing persecution. The U.S. has accepted more than 4,000 white South African refugees and is considering expanding the program.
